page: Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 5669 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

The x86_64 architecture CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. It lacks Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache.

In benchmark testing, the server achieves top-tier (top 10%) results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as well as PassMark CPU, encryption, and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 10% for small-block cached reads and large-block uncached writes, though uncached large-block reads drop slightly to the top 25%. The low memory density of 2.0 GB per core represents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute power and local storage capacity over massive RAM arrays.

Database operations and key-value stores perform exceptionally well, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks both ranking in the top 10%. The server also demonstrates top-tier performance in static web serving and single-threaded compression tasks. For machine learning, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small, medium, and large LLM models, though prompt processing for large 70B models falls to average. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, storage-intensive workloads like high-throughput database hosting, web serving, and parallel data processing that do not require high memory-per-core ratios.
description: The Microsoft Azure D96alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs. Part of the Daldsv7 family, this low-memory instance provides 192.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) alongside a substantial 5669 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmark results place its CPU compute, cryptographic execution, and database operations in the top 10% tier. While its low memory-to-CPU ratio is a tradeoff for RAM-heavy applications, its high-speed processor and large local storage make it highly efficient for compute-bound tasks. It is optimized for high-throughput database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression.
